channel.title: The New Yorker — Reporting
channel.description: Latest reporting from The New Yorker

item.title: Why Immigration Agents Don’t Quit in Protest
item.description: How a culture of dehumanization and denial keepsICEand Border Patrol personnel “at war with an enemy that does not fight back.”

item.title: An Exiled Filmmaker’s Unsparing View of Contemporary Russia
item.description: Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur” is the first independent feature to portray Russian life during the war with Ukraine.

item.title: An N.B.A. Player Got Hooked on Sports Betting. Soon, He Became the Bet
item.description: Jontay Porter got deep into FanDuel, and in debt to the wrong people. The only way out, it seemed, was to gamble on himself.

item.title: What It Takes to Save a Town from Wildfire
item.description: Catastrophic blazes are exposing the limits of individual precautions. Can communities build a system of collective defense?

item.title: The Ubiquitous Melancholy of Max Richter
item.description: The composer’s song “On the Nature of Daylight” has popped up in countless sob fests including “Arrival” and “Hamnet.” With billions of streams, he’s become one of the most popular and successful composers of our time.

item.title: Can American Socialism Survive Its Success?
item.description: The movement has often seen its ideas flourish as its organizations withered. Will today’s resurgence follow the same course?

item.title: Jesse Eisenberg Can’t Help Overthinking It
item.description: His new film, “The Debut,” which stars Julianne Moore as a housewife turned egomaniacal actress, puts self-invented drama center stage.

item.title: The Buddhist A.I. Sect That Wants to Take Over Silicon Valley
item.description: MAPLE promises to teach us how to live in the age of A.I. Its secret mission is much stranger.

item.title: Would You Dissect a Human Body?
item.description: A doctor visits a lab where yoga teachers and massage therapists cut into cadavers.

item.title: Venezuela’s Collaborator-in-Chief
item.description: Delcy Rodríguez and the new American imperialism.
